problems.problem: Eight block-level record counts were shown as FACT under 'how I searched [1] to [7]' with no Sources entry. The cited logs are the combined searches, which do not contain these numbers. Corrected only at msg 22. This fails G4 and drives M4 to 0.
problems.cause: The kit renders each search card with its own Sources line (scripts/cards.json). Prompt section 3 says 'close with one line Sources', so the agent stripped the per-card lines (scripts/cards_nosrc.json) and retyped one Sources line by hand, which dropped L000053/54/56/57/64-67.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.merge_cards(cards) to renumber every card's citations into one Sources line. Make k.verify_reply(text) reject a number inside a FACT block that has no [n]. Prompt section 3: append 'When you show several search cards, merge their Sources with k.merge_cards; never delete a citation a card carries.'

problems.problem: The search strategy the persona wanted came after 4 review tables (29 rows), 7 search cards and 325 prose words. The persona could not pick it out and had to ask (report for msg 21: 'couldn't quickly pick out the actual search strategy').
problems.cause: Prompt Step 3 asks for every review, every search card and the coverage DRAFT in one reply, with no rule on order or size; the 180-word cap covers prose only.
problems.fix: Prompt Step 3: 'Lead with three lines: how many reviews bear on the focus, and what they cover, leave uncovered or leave unknown. Then one compact table (search, source, looks for, records [n]) with the strings. Then the reviews, at most 10 rows per group, the rest offered as "show reviews".' Kit: k.search_summary_table(log_ids).

problems.problem: Asked 'what was the search strategy?', the assistant printed all seven strings, every block table and the syntax glossary again (265 prose words), where the persona card expects a compact recap. Report for msg 23: 're-dumped all seven search strings and every block table'.
problems.cause: The prompt allows repeating on request but defines no compact form. The kit tracks session.json glossary_shown but nothing uses it.
problems.fix: Prompt section 3: 'When asked to see something already shown, give its compact form: one row per search with its string; do not re-explain syntax already in glossary_shown.' Kit: k.search_summary(compact=True), which skips glossary entries already shown.

problems.problem: The Step 3 Your turn bundles three questions in one ask, outside intake: do the reviews change your focus, clinical justification, expected impact. It is repeated at msg 28. The persona would answer only the first (report for msg 27).
problems.cause: Prompt Step 3 writes them as one ask: 'Ask whether this changes how the team sees its focus, and for the clinical justification and expected impact.'
problems.fix: Prompt Step 3: 'Ask one at a time: first "Do these reviews change your focus? yes / no / how" with example replies; then the clinical justification; then the expected impact.'

problems.problem: The DRAFT says three headings (Adipose Tissue; Muscle, Skeletal; Asia) were not looked up, which implies the others were. The log holds only four lookups (L000045-52: SGLT2 inhibitors, body composition, weight loss, Asian people), so Body Weight, Obesity and Overweight were not looked up either.
problems.cause: No kit function reports which [Mesh] terms in a strategy were looked up, so the agent described its own process from memory.
problems.fix: Kit: k.mesh_coverage(strategy), listing each [Mesh] term with its lookup log id or 'not looked up'. Prompt R6/R7: 'Say which headings were checked only by quoting k.mesh_coverage.'

problems.problem: '9 of the 16 are in type 2 diabetes only', '4 of them published in 2026' and the protocols' 'latest from 2022' appear in no saved code output; need_A_summary.json lacks them. Draft L000072 had hand-typed counts ('10 of 16'; '3 of 13 report weight') that later corrections replaced (L000080, L000084).
problems.cause: The analysis script emits only some of the counts the reply states, and k.draft accepts any digits in free text, so R7 is unenforced.
problems.fix: Kit: k.draft(text, numbers_from=<summary.json>) that rejects any number not equal to a value in the cited summary. Prompt R7: 'Before writing a sentence with a literature number, add that number as a key in the analysis script's summary.'

problems.problem: 'Waiting on you' went 2 at msg 14, 3 at msg 16 and 1 at msg 18, although each reply asked one thing. Report for msg 17: 'up from 2... nothing explains the change'.
problems.cause: Kit _waiting() counts every proposed decision (Individual Motivation and Team's Purpose) plus each open blocking question, including the purpose certification that had not yet been asked.
problems.fix: Kit _waiting(): count only blocking questions asked and still unanswered plus the one certification currently requested. Prompt status-line text: 'Waiting on you = the number of things in this Your turn'.

problems.problem: The Done line reported 'This may change what you approved for Individual Motivation (when an undisclosed individual motivation conflicts...)'. This was for a solo member whose motivation is disclosed and certified. The persona read it as jargon and could not tell whether to act (report for msg 27).
problems.cause: Kit trace() reports every flow from the changed decision that reaches a certified decision without checking the flow's condition, and the prompt asks for the trace in the Done line.
problems.fix: Model and kit: give flow 2 the condition 'a member's motivation is undisclosed'; trace() drops it when team.yaml shows every member as disclosed. Prompt Done-line rule: 'When a traced flow needs no action, write "Checked: nothing to change".'

problems.problem: No plan map was shown when work moved to Step 3 early. The map shown at msg 24 still marks Step 3 'next', waiting on nobody, while the status line says '(Step 3 started early)'. The persona was unsure which step counted (reports for msgs 21 and 23).
problems.cause: Kit plan_map() ignores _early(), and the prompt's list of plan-map events does not include an early start.
problems.fix: Kit plan_map(): show the early step as 'started early (open: <items>)', with the earlier step's pending item in Waiting on. Prompt: add 'an early start' to the events that show the map.

problems.problem: 8 of 12 turns exceed the prompt's own 180-word prose cap (median 189.5; 325 at msg 20; 287 at msg 28). The 12-row plan map is printed 7 times. Every Done line ends 'Nothing you have approved is affected'. The email and model-name ask is repeated at msg 18, the turn right after msg 14. Persona reports for msgs 9, 15 and 19 complain about length and repetition.
problems.cause: The pre-send check states the cap, but the kit does not count prose. The prompt shows the full map at many events. Nothing records that a 'When convenient' item was already asked.
problems.fix: Kit: k.check_reply(text) that counts prose words, flags 'When convenient' items already asked (by question log id) and flags a repeated map. Prompt: 'Between map events show one line "Steps: 1 done · 2 now · 3 next"; ask each When convenient item once and list it again only in the pause summary; omit "Nothing you have approved is affected" when nothing was approved.'

judge.strengths: Certification handling was flawless. The assistant refused a bare 'Certify', asked only for the reason, never suggested one, kept the certified wording identical to what was last shown, and committed each certification. It added no aim or focus of its own. Purpose options appeared only after free answers, with none pre-selected, and the vague 'all of it' answer got exactly the two prescribed probes. Every status line was kit-generated and correct. The early start of Step 3 was announced, flagged in the status line and logged with the open item named. Logging is complete: 95 records, 31 raw responses with sha256, flow traces and per-certification commits. Every literature number shown reproduces from saved files, and two wrong hand-typed draft counts were corrected by code before display. Scope was reported honestly: titles and abstracts only, end dates read from the abstracts with 'unknown' where none was given, and 'non-diabetic' explained as a text check rather than a block. The searches stated their date bounds, and the registers not searched were named with who can search them. The assistant declined OpenAlex's embedded invitation to request a key with the user's email. The pause put the summary and the plan map in the chat and packaged the workspace only then. The first literature FACT came at planning turn 8, with no mid-session file pointers.
